quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Leave the road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle needs more distance to stop, give yourself more space to react.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Skip checking the tire pressure.
Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
Assume the lender checked the brakes for you.
Ride cautiously and keep extra space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride cautiously and keep extra space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Check a borrowed motorcycle the same way you would check your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and give yourself extra stopping distance.

questions.question: When should you keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To hide from the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space when conditions make stopping difficult. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic. Extra space gives you more time to react.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Speed up to shake them off.
Call the local police.
Ride on the shoulder.
Let them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and allow them to get ahead of you. Speeding up only increases danger.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Speed up.
Use only the front brake.
Avoid sudden movements.
Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes smoothly, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily spots, shaded areas, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these have less traction.

questions.question: What is the correct foot position when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Drag your feet on the ground.
Point your toes downward.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag them or point toes down, as this can catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly.

questions.question: What rule applies when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may finish a pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You should use your horn to slow the other driver down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen within the posted speed limits and only in areas where passing is legal and safe.

questions.question: Where should you ride when following a car?

options.text: Anywhere in the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
In the position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: How is the accelerator controlled on a motorcycle?

options.text: With the right hand.
With the left hand.
With the right foot.
With the left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand.
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and you control it with your right hand.

questions.question: How do you make the shortest and safest stop?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Lock up the front tire.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes smoothly and evenly without locking either tire. This gives you the shortest and safest stop.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:

options.text: Meet Department of Transportation standards.
Look sturdy.
Be inexpensive.
Be your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meet Department of Transportation standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Sit with your arms supporting your weight instead of steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit far back so you have to stretch to reach the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance during turns. Use your arms to steer, not to support yourself. Sit close enough that your arms bend slightly at the handlebars. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two people.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not require the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two people.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat designed for two riders. It should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?

options.text: THC
TMJ
MRT
AAP

questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: The main active substance in marijuana is called THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

questions.question: Before riding, you should check your tires for all of the following, except:

options.text: Air pressure.
Tread.
General wear.
Flexibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Check your tire air pressure, general wear, and tread before every ride.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?

options.text: Near the left footrest.
Near the right footrest.
On the left handlebar grip.
On the right handlebar grip.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handlebar grip.
questions.explanation: The throttle is usually on the right handlebar grip. Know where all controls are before riding.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, Execute
Scan, Error, Elevate
Stop, Extend, Enter
Share, Extra, Escalate

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, Execute
questions.explanation: The SEE strategy helps you make safe decisions while riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Should be avoided.
Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only happen in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.
Ride faster.
Ride on the shoulder.
Pull off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, rest every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Stop wheels from skidding and locking up.
Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Apply brakes automatically.
Alert you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop wheels from skidding and locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel skidding and lock-up during hard braking. When you apply full brake pressure, sensors detect if a wheel might lock. The system then releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep maximum braking power.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.
Be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good jackets and pants cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but be loose enough to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials work best to protect you if you crash.

questions.question: You can increase your visibility by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
Not using your turn signal.
Wearing dark clothing.
Waving at people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can increase visibility by wearing bright or reflective clothing. Adding extra lights to your motorcycle, using turn signals, and flashing your brake light also help other drivers see you.

questions.question: If the chain or belt of your motorcycle breaks, you will:

options.text: Get a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Lose power to the rear wheel suddenly.
Lose power to the front wheel suddenly.
Get a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose power to the rear wheel suddenly.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, you will lose power to the rear wheel immediately.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Increase their speed.
Reduce their speed.
Make sudden moves.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Sudden moves can make your motorcycle skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are too small to worry about.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular part of your scanning routine.
